title: Principal Robotic Controls Engineer
description:
WHO WE ARE

Aurelius is the autonomous directed energy company.

We are a group of engineers, operators, and company patriots building American-made, laser-based counter-UAS systems that neutralize aerial threats.

Archimedes, our autonomous laser turret, combines a high-power laser with radar and machine vision to find, track, and defeat small drones. We design in San Francisco, manufacture in Detroit, and test onsite, on our own cUAS range.

THE ROLE

You'll own beam control and tracking for Archimedes.

That covers the nested pointing architecture, the estimators that fuse radar, EO/IR, and inertial data, the jitter and latency budgets, and the analysis that says what the system can and cannot hit before range testing. You'll derive the loops, run them in our in-house simulator, get them on hardware within days, and test them against maneuvering drones on the outdoor range. You'll partner with perception, optics, mechanical, and software, and be the senior technical voice on controls decisions.

MUST-HAVES

- PhD-level depth in control theory and estimation, enough to derive and defend the architecture, not just tune it. An MS plus a research-grade record of theory work put on fielded hardware can substitute.

- Closed loops on precision pointing, tracking, or stabilization hardware that had to meet a measured spec in the field

- Hands-on system identification and plant modeling against real structural dynamics, with models that predicted what the hardware then did

- Shipped real-time loops in C++ on embedded targets, or worked closely with the engineers who did, and understand what latency and quantization do to your margins

- U.S. citizenship, required for export control

FIRST 6 MONTHS

- Design the beam director control architecture: coarse gimbal and fine steering loop structure, bandwidth allocation, and the handoff between stages

- Build target state estimation that fuses radar cue, EO/IR track, and inertial data into a predicted aimpoint, with latency compensation designed in

- Allocate a pointing error budget (jitter, bias, latency, atmosphere) across the system and test it on the outdoor range

- Build plant models from frequency and time domain ID of the gimbal, mirror, and structure, running in the in-house simulator and validated hardware-in-the-loop

- Mentor the controls team and lead technical reviews that catch risk in controls, estimation, and sensor integration

NICE TO HAVES

- Directed energy weapon or high energy laser program experience

- Adaptive optics, wavefront sensing, or atmospheric propagation and beam wander modeling

- MATLAB/Simulink to production code, or Python and C++ toolchains for control design and hardware-in-the-loop

- An active security clearance, or the ability to get one

NOT A FIT IF

- Your controls experience is PID tuning from a block library without the theory to explain why it works

- You're a theorist who has never closed a loop on real hardware, or a manager without recent hands-on work

- You need remote or hybrid work

HOW WE WORK

At Aurelius we work what we call, 5+X. Our core operating hours are 5 days a week, Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm Pacific Time.

The X is the honest acknowledgment that hard work sometimes takes more. That can be late nights and weekends during sprints and ramp-up periods or conferences, deployments, and events when the mission calls for it.

1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.

- Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
